parsed.why: Strong state anti-discrimination covering public accommodations, hate-crime enhancement, no bathroom ban, and a care shield; national passport, entry and federal-facility exposure still cap it in Elevated Risk.
Low-risk tier but protections are baseline: 2013 anti-discrimination and hate crimes, no bathroom ban; missing X markers, shield law and unresolved panic-defence bill leave it just above parent.
Most Protective tier with shield law, anti-discrimination, hate crimes, X markers and custody treatment by gender identity; national border and federal-facility rules remain the main exposure.
Most Protective with broad anti-discrimination, constitutional amendment, hate crimes, shield law, gender-neutral bathrooms and repealed loitering law; national border and custody rules still apply.

Hostile state layer: youth, Medicaid and prison care bans, surgical birth-certificate rule, no gender-identity non-discrimination; hate-crime coverage and no bathroom ban only partly offset, below parent.
